mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates strengthening economic demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances following two consecutive quarters of GDP growth, or if the correlation between GDP growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the same month signals strong consumer demand and labor market health, which typically boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases & UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of RSAFS increase and UNRATE decrease on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate robust economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as borrowing costs decrease and economic activity is stimulated.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the same month signals strong demand in the housing market and labor market health, which typically boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases & UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST increase and UNRATE decrease on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
